subject: Intermittent inference failures after maintenance — customer readout & actions
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinepayments.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance - impact to inference jobs

Diego —

We're seeing a steady stream of failed inference jobs and session resync errors since last night's maintenance window. Approximately 3-4% of requests fail with a 502-style error and many of our longer-running streaming sessions drop mid-response.

Impacts:
- Checkout recommendation engine timeouts (affecting a subset of EU customers routed through our US region)
- Increased tail latency and retries in our workers

We've collected logs and a sample session dump and attached them to this message. Can you confirm whether this is related to the rolling restart you ran? We need an ETA for a fix and any immediate mitigation we can apply on our side.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform, Skyline Payments
ops@skylinepayments.com

Attachment: skyline-sample-session-0620.log (text)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after maintenance - impact to inference jobs

Marta —

Thanks for the note and for attaching logs. We saw elevated errors in the hosted fleet coincident with the rolling restart that completed at ~01:10 UTC. We're opening a dedicated incident channel and I wanted to confirm a few quick items:

1) Can you paste the exact request IDs for a few failed attempts (we have some, but cross-matching speeds debugging)
2) Are your workers pinning model versions or using the floating catalog variant (we'll need this to determine whether a model binary swap was involved)

Immediate mitigation we can try from our side: pause further restarts in the impacted zone and roll back a config change that was applied as part of the maintenance. From your side, increasing client-side retry backoff from 2s to 8s will reduce user-facing errors while we investigate.

I've looped in Laura (runtime lead) and Hannah (ops) to drive the fix. We'll follow up with a concise RCA and action plan by EOD PST.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwoodinference.com

--

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, support@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-recovery readout: root cause, timeline, and customer actions (summary)

Marta / Skyline team —

Summary (short):
We completed investigation and mitigations this morning. Root cause: a subtle regression in our custom GPU driver combined with a recent runtime change to the session serialization path caused KV-cache snapshots to be written with a missing checksum in a narrow window during a rolling restart. When a worker attempted to resume an in-flight streaming session, the KV deserializer rejected the snapshot and the runtime initiated a session resync that the client did not always tolerate, producing the observed failures and dropped streams.

Why it happened:
- Maintenance included a rolling restart across the serving pool to apply a minor runtime change to memory accounting.
- A new driver build (automatic via our build pipeline) contained a regression that made snapshot flush non-atomic for a small subset of models with large KV sizes.
- The combination of those two events exposed the edge case where a snapshot could be persisted with a null checksum and later rejected by the deserializer.

Timeline (high level):
- 2028-06-20 00:58 UTC — maintenance rolling restart begins in us-west-2 zone
- 2028-06-20 01:09 UTC — elevated 502s and session resync traces appear in monitoring
- 2028-06-20 01:30 UTC — on-call paged; rollback of runtime memory-accounting change started
- 2028-06-20 02:15 UTC — driver identified as likely cause; hotfix driver build prepared
- 2028-06-20 03:05 UTC — hotfix staged to a canary subset; no further regressions observed there
- 2028-06-20 06:40 UTC — hotfix promoted; full fleet remediation completed and error rates returned to baseline

Customer impact: ~2.8% token-level failure rate for affected requests in the 01:00-06:40 UTC window. Most customers saw transient failures with automatic retries recovering in <30s; a small subset that relied on long-lived streaming sessions observed truncated responses.

Actions we committed (owners) and verification steps: 
- Deploy verified hotfix driver across remaining regions (Laura Bennett) — already completed for us-west-2; scheduled for eu-west-1 by 2028-06-21 02:00 UTC
- Add pre-rollout checksum verification and stronger invariant assertions to snapshot writes (Runtime team — Laura) — PR in review; expected merge by 2028-06-22
- Add a short-term client retry guidance note and sample SDK patch to gracefully handle resyncs (Developer Experience — Diego) — attached sample SDK change and README snippet
- Operational guardrails: block auto-driver promotions without canary window and introduce a rollout circuit breaker for snapshot-affecting changes (Hannah Schmitt) — change scheduled and included in the attached action ledger
- Customer verification: run the attached smoke test harness against a small subset of your traffic and confirm no resync errors (Skyline ops) — steps in event-timeline-20280620.csv

Attachments (zipped in the Drive link):
- rsca-20280620-summary.pdf (this RCA summary)
- event-timeline-20280620.csv (sample request IDs and verification steps)
- mitigation-action-ledger-20280620.xlsx (owners, due dates, status)
- sample-sdk-retry-patch.diff (one-line patch and README snippet)

Compensation / credits: We understand the operational impact. Our support team will open a compensation review if you want to pursue usage credits for the window — I've flagged this with our account team.

Next steps: Please run the verification harness and reply to this thread with the sample request IDs that still fail (if any). We'll keep the channel open for the next 72 hours and will provide an automated verification report by EOD Wednesday.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority and will follow up with the merged PR and rollout notes once available.

Best regards,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stubs: rsca-20280620-summary.pdf (pdf), event-timeline-20280620.csv (csv), mitigation-action-ledger-20280620.xlsx (xlsx), sample-sdk-retry-patch.diff (text)

Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-recovery readout: root cause, timeline, and customer actions (summary)

Marta —

Quick technical follow-up: we've merged the runtime assertion PR to block writes with missing checksums and patched the driver on the entire us-west-2 fleet. The patch includes a conservative write barrier; we validated with a targeted smoke run (attached results).

Requested verification steps for Skyline:
1) Run the attached smoke harness (event-timeline CSV) against a 1% traffic shadow for 2 hours
2) Report any request IDs that surface a resync or checksum rejection
3) If clean, please confirm and we'll mark the action as Verified in the ledger and schedule the eu-west-1 push

I'll also coordinate a short postmortem notes doc for your internal audit team if you need packaged evidence for compliance.

Laura Bennett
Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
